item.title: Physics Colloquium - The Twisted Genome: How DNA Torsion Shapes Genome Function — Wed Oct 21, 3:30 PM — None
item.description:
Because DNA is a double helix, the molecular machines that read, copy, and package the genome inevitably twist it. Yet the consequences of this twisting have remained difficult to study. To address this challenge, we developed new single-molecule tools to manipulate and measure DNA torsion. These studies reveal that torsional stress is not merely a byproduct of molecular activity but a fundamental regulator of genome function, highlighting the important roles of mechanics and topology in biology.
Source: Duke University

** Join us for the opening reception at CDS on Thursday, October 22, from 5:30 - 7 p.m. Come back for a free family event on Saturday, October 24, 11 a.m. - 3 p.m. **

Register here: https://www.eventbrite.com/e/structure-sign-and-play-in-the-age-of-ai-tickets-2002461745987?aff=oddtdtcreator
Structure, Sign, and Play in the Age of AI marks sixty years since Derrida's 1966 lecture at Johns Hopkins, the moment structuralism supposedly gave way to poststructuralism. Structuralism is currently experiencing a revival. Contemporary AI technologies depend on data sets so large that the structuralist hypothesis-Ferdinand de Saussure's notion of meaning as a differential "web" of signifiers-seems almost realized. Yet the age of AI is most commonly characterized as "postmodern," filled with "floating signifiers" that are "ungrounded" and lacking any clear relationship to truth. item.title: Wanting Children: Family-Planning Policies and the Engineering of America's Population — Thu Oct 22, 12:00 PM — SSRI-Gross Hall 270
item.description:
This talk is based on my recently published book, Wanting Children: Family-Planning Policies and the Engineering of America's Population (University of Chicago Press). Unlike most of the world, U.S. family-planning policy has focused almost exclusively on limiting fertility, with little attention to supporting people who want to have children. I trace the historical and political roots of this asymmetry and argue for a more balanced approach to population policy - one that takes seriously the needs of those who want to become parents. Drawing on population research, I'll discuss what a more supportive fertility policy should look like and why it matters for the future of the American population.
Source: Duke University

item.description:
Abstract: The exponential rise in the production and use of polymers, particularly in single use applications, has led to a dramatic increase in their environmental prevalence and problems with plastic waste management. One necessary component of the solution to this challenge is developing plastics that degrade more effectively in the environment, be it due to accidental release, composting, or presence in sewage. While this need has been widely known for decades, slow innovation cycles, inertia in our materials systems, and cost and performance barriers have dramatically limited the number of new materials that come to market.
This talk will present a vision for workflows of the future that can be used to accelerate materials innovation through a combination of high-throughput measurement, data science, and machine learning and will apply these workflows to facilitate the discovery of new materials that improve sustainability. item.title: Switch Theatre Company Presents August Wilson's Radio Golf — Thu Oct 22, 7:00 PM — Durham Arts Council
item.description:
Harmond Wilks is on the verge of becoming Pittsburgh’s first Black mayor, and his ambitious redevelopment project for the Hill District – including a new golf course – promises economic growth and a new future. But his plans may be derailed by a single rundown house owned by long time resident “Old Joe” Barlow, who may have a deeper connection to Harmond’s past. Along with his upwardly-mobile business partner Roosevelt, his public relations mastermind wife Mame, and street-smart handyman Sterling, Harmond is forced to confront the cost of progress, the meaning of legacy, and the value of community. The riveting final chapter of August Wilson’s 10-play American Century Cycle, Radio Golf is a compelling and timely drama that challenges us to consider what we are willing to sacrifice for the sake of the future.
